mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate of 4.33% is historically low, and periods of low interest rates have been associated with positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to compressed discount rates on equity cash flows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of all 20-day windows over the past 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces corporate earnings potential, leading to negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1400 and industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 103, it indicates weak demand and strong supply, signaling economic slowdown and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where HOUST < 1400 AND INDPRO > 103.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (defined as FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% and sustained for 3 months), higher discount rates and reduced liquidity cause negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances during monetary tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: The current industrial production level of 103.9867 (above 2017 base of 100) indicates economic growth, which historically has been associated with positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of time when INDPRO > 100.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 1400, it signals weak consumer demand and reduced economic activity, leading to negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST < 1400.

mechanism_narrative: When labor market weakness (PAYEMS growth < 0.5% monthly) coincides with rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS increase > 0.2% in 3 months), dual economic stress causes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth < 0.5% AND FEDFUNDS increase > 0.2% in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS growth < 0.5% AND FEDFUNDS increase > 0.2% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: During demand recession regimes (defined as GDPC1 growth < 1% quarterly and CPIAUCSL annualized < 2%), reduced consumer spending and weak economic growth cause negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where GDPC1 growth < 1% AND CPIAUCSL annualized < 2%.
